domain_label: Movie Studio — Persona Storyworld & Series Design for a Classic-Luxurious Two-Persona Reel Account
purpose: A method for the storyworld-level work a series designer reasons about when running one male and one female classic-luxurious Instagram persona: mapping want (the visible per-reel pursuit) against need (the value revealed across the series), locking the quiet Patrician status register per Han, Nunes & Dreze (2010), deploying mystery and aloofness as luxury devices without ever entering the closed real-person-likeness lane, building a named recurring-format library with per-format loop-vs-open-loop ending choices, running the duo as parallel lives punctuated by scarce crossovers, directing voiceover pace/pitch/pause while carrying the owner word 'phonics' as a named [UNKNOWN] speech-to-text artifact, and enforcing series-bible discipline so every post stays genre-consistent — with every empirical claim carried under the grounding file's FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tags and no engagement number, platform policy, or study result invented.
assumptions: no live account analytics are supplied; every score is a heuristic prior and every engagement or psychology claim is quoted from the grounding research file (story_and_emotion.md) with its honesty tag, never re-derived or upgraded here

screenwriting craft (want/need, hero's journey as series skeleton, loop mechanics, recurring formats) is human craft doctrine tagged [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine] in the grounding file and stays doctrine here, not laboratory fact

the much-cited 85%-muted-viewing figure is a 2016 Digiday publisher-reported range (FACT-of-attribution, ESTIMATE-of-generality) and is used only as a design constraint (design for muted first exposure), never as a current platform metric
the owner word 'phonics' is an [UNKNOWN] speech-to-text artifact; the voice-delivery reading (pace, pitch, pause) is an interpretation carried as such, revocable on owner clarification

Higgsfield model names, ids, parameters and media roles belong to the surface-enumeration file and are deliberately absent here; this KB hands delivery and format direction to those specialists without naming tools
exclusions: per-reel shot grammar, stitch transitions, edit rhythm and camera moves (camera & editing specialist), and the intra-reel hook/setup/escalation/payoff beat math beyond what series design needs from ending modes
FACS action-unit phrasing for image/video prompts and the basic-emotions debate mechanics (expression/prompting KB); this KB only inherits 'restraint reads as class' as an aloofness device
posting cadence, timing, and platform ranking-signal tactics (media-manager domain); story design only aligns its emotional register with shareability and hands off

legal analysis of celebrity likeness, right of publicity, or platform policy — the likeness lane is simply CLOSED here: no guidance exists or may be authored for evoking a specific real person while hiding the face
voice tool selection, model parameters, or audio generation mechanics (audio/soundtrack specialist); this KB supplies only the delivery direction those tools are prompted with

competency_questions.question: Why is the account, not the individual reel, the real narrative unit, and what happens to classic long-form structure at reel scale?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCOUNT_AS_NARRATIVE_UNIT states that at 15-60s only hook, escalation and climactic payoff/loop survive per reel (Freytag's falling action and denouement are cut), that the hero's-journey monomyth is far too long for one reel and survives only as a series-level skeleton where each post is one beat, and that arcs, subplots and the need-revelation therefore migrate up to the feed level

competency_questions.question: How do want and need map onto a luxury persona operation, and at what timescale is each shown?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERSONA_WANT_DEFINITION states the want is the external, conscious, plot-driving visible pursuit shown per reel (destination, acquisition, achievement) and PERSONA_NEED_ARC states the need is the internal value the brand stands for (freedom, self-mastery, taste) revealed across the series, that want drives plot while need drives the arc, and that the need is what makes an audience bond rather than just envy — all tagged craft doctrine

competency_questions.question: What does Han, Nunes & Dreze's brand-prominence research imply for the classic-luxurious register, and which signaling group must the personas embody?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUIET_STATUS_SIGNALING names the 2010 Journal of Marketing paper, the brand-prominence construct, the four groups (Patricians, Parvenus, Proletarians, Poseurs), the empirical finding that loud prominently-branded goods averaged cheaper than quiet ones in the 465-handbag study, and concludes the classic-luxurious register is the Patrician quiet-signal position: texture, cut and setting over visible branding

competency_questions.question: How do mystery and aloofness function as luxury-persona devices, and what concrete visual grammar implements them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MYSTERY_ALOOFNESS_DEVICES states scarcity of self-disclosure as a status signal (craft doctrine) and lists the devices: restrained near-micro expression, gaze control, not explaining, and controlled reveal such as back-to-camera or partial obscuring, noting restraint reads as class while broad expression reads as trying-too-hard

competency_questions.question: Where is the hard boundary on non-revelation devices with respect to real people?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LIKENESS_LANE_GUARD states the lane is closed: obscured-face and non-revelation grammar applies only to the two original personas, no styling, context or caption may be designed to evoke a specific real person while hiding the face, and the legal analysis lives in the legal research file — this KB carries only the prohibition

competency_questions.question: What recurring formats should the two personas cycle through, and why do named repeatable formats matter?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RECURRING_FORMAT_LIBRARY names the five grounded formats (come-with-me POV arrival, transformation/reveal, quote-over-cinematic, a-day/a-place, dual-persona interplay) and states the two rationales: recurring formats build viewer expectation and lower production cost, with every format legible muted

competency_questions.question: How do open-loop endings and numbered series convert curiosity into follows, and when does a hard seamless loop win instead?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OPEN_LOOP_EPISODIC_HOOKS grounds the open loop in Loewenstein's 1994 information-gap theory (curiosity as deprivation from a perceived, fillable knowledge gap) and states numbered series give an explicit reason to follow and return; ENDING_MODE_CHOICE states seamless looping is a documented watch-time tactic (replay without noticing) and assigns hard loop to ambient formats and open loop to narrative series, per format

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AWE_SHARE_ALIGNMENT cites Berger & Milkman 2012 (high-arousal emotions, awe foremost among positives, drive virality; low-arousal sadness suppresses it; held controlling for surprise, interest, usefulness, placement) and concludes luxury travel/architecture reveals are awe machines, so the series should lean into scale and reveal while distribution tactics stay with the media manager

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DUO_PARALLEL_LIVES states each persona carries its own want/need arc in the shared classic-luxurious genre (craft-doctrine design, grounded in the dual-persona-interplay format), and DUO_CROSSOVER_EPISODES states crossovers are scarce paired events that reward followers of both feeds and must not become the majority of posts

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SILENT_LEGIBILITY_CONSTRAINT quotes the ~85%-muted figure with its full caveat (Digiday 2016, publisher-reported range, FACT-of-attribution / ESTIMATE-of-generality, not a current universal metric) and states the load-bearing implication that meaning must be carried visually and by on-screen text; VOICEOVER_ENHANCEMENT_RULE states the voiceover is an enhancement for the minority who unmute, spoken content must be captioned, and a sound-on payoff is a bonus never a dependency

competency_questions.question: What must the series bible contain, and how do recurring signatures and the per-episode gate keep the feed genre-consistent?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSISTENCY_SIGNATURES states recurring visual signatures (a color grade, a location type, a recurring wardrobe piece or object) are the narrative glue that lets disconnected reels read as one ongoing story; SERIES_BIBLE_DISCIPLINE lists the bible's contents (per-persona want/need, quiet register rules, format library, ending-mode table, signature set, arc position, honesty tags on every empirical claim); EPISODE_GONOGO_GATE composes the pre-post checklist

glossary.definition: Craft-doctrine pair: the want is the external, conscious, plot-driving goal; the need is the internal, often unconscious lesson or value — want drives plot, need drives the arc [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine - No Film School; Scott Myers, Go Into The Story]. In the persona operation: want = the visible per-reel pursuit, need = the value the brand stands for, revealed across posts.

How conspicuous a luxury good's logo/mark is; introduced by Han, Nunes & Dreze (2010), Journal of Marketing 74:15-30, with the finding that loud, prominently-branded status goods averaged cheaper than quiet ones in a study of 465 Gucci/LV handbags [FACT - source 15 in the grounding file].

The wealthy-low-need-for-status quadrant of the Han/Nunes/Dreze taxonomy: pay a premium for quiet signals only insiders recognize. The owner's classic-luxurious aesthetic maps to this register: understated tailoring, materials-and-craft over branding, no loud logos [FACT taxonomy; ESTIMATE application].

A non-disclosure move that reads as exclusivity: restrained near-micro expression, gaze control (looking away or a cool direct gaze), not explaining the image, controlled reveal (back-to-camera, partial obscuring). Scarcity of self-disclosure as status signal is craft doctrine, not measured fact [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine].

An ending that deliberately leaves an information gap unfilled ('part 2', an unresolved beat) to drive comments and follows; grounded in Loewenstein (1994) information-gap theory of curiosity, Psychological Bulletin 116(1):75-98 [FACT theory; ESTIMATE application].

Designing the final frame to flow back into the first so the restart is invisible; a documented watch-time tactic because viewers rewatch without noticing [FACT - documented tactic, source 10]. The 7-10s optimal loop length claim is a marketing blog figure — directional only [ESTIMATE].

A named, repeatable reel template the personas cycle through (come-with-me POV arrival, transformation/reveal, quote-over-cinematic, a-day/a-place, dual-persona interplay); builds viewer expectation and lowers production cost [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine].

The single governance document that fixes each persona's want/need, the quiet-luxury register rules, the format library with per-format ending modes, the signature set, the duo arc map and crossover cadence, and the honesty tag of every empirical claim the operation relies on — the discipline that keeps the feed genre-consistent classic-luxurious [ESTIMATE / craft discipline].

A paired or complementary post in which the male and female personas appear in one storyline; grounded in the dual-persona-interplay recurring format, treated as a scarce event so the parallel storylines stay distinct [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine].

The voiceover speaking-rate target: conversational English averages ~150 wpm (National Center for Voice and Speech), adults sit 120-150 wpm in conversation, audiobook/podcast narration runs ~150-160 wpm [FACT - source 16]; the reel-specific 140-160 wpm aim with <130 ponderous / >170 rushed is craft calibration [ESTIMATE].

nodes.definition: Fix the frame the whole KB reasons in: the account is the real narrative unit and individual reels are beats. At 15-60s the only reliable per-reel survivors of classic structure are hook, escalation and a climactic payoff/loop — Freytag's five parts (exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, denouement; Die Technik des Dramas, 1863 [FACT - definition]) lose their entire back half, since a 15-30s reel cannot afford a wind-down [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]. The Campbell/Vogler hero's journey is far too long for one reel; what survives is (a) a single beat can BE a reel (the threshold crossing = the car pulling out of the gate; the reward = the summit reveal) and (b) the full arc spreads across the series — each post is one beat, the account is the journey [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]. Denouement, subplot and multi-beat arcs therefore migrate up to the feed level, which is exactly the level this KB designs.

included: the account-as-narrative-unit frame
what survives of Freytag and the monomyth at reel scale
the arc-migrates-up principle
excluded: per-reel hook/setup/escalation/payoff mechanics (camera/editing and micro-story domain)
posting cadence (media manager)

pros.claim: Framing the account as the story lets disconnected 15-60s posts accumulate into an arc no single reel could carry
pros.example: spreading ordinary-world, threshold, trials and reward beats across a month of posts so long-term followers experience a journey

cons.claim: Series-level structure is invisible to a first-touch viewer, so it can never excuse a weak individual reel
cons.example: a mid-arc post that only makes sense to followers bleeding the non-follower majority who see it cold

failure_modes: designing each reel as a self-contained mini-film and leaving the feed with no spine beyond disconnected flexes
porting full three-act or five-part structure into one reel and wasting seconds on a denouement no viewer stays for
acceptance_tests: the analysis states that only hook, escalation and payoff/loop survive per reel, that Freytag's falling action and denouement are cut, and that the hero's journey functions only as a series-level skeleton with each post as one beat
revisit_triggers: the platform format length changes materially from the 15-60s band
audience data shows followers versus non-followers responding differently to arc-dependent posts
a new long-form surface (e.g. multi-minute video) enters the operation

base.update_signal: a format-length change or follower/non-follower response split changes where the arc should live

nodes.definition: Define each persona's want: the external, conscious, plot-driving goal [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine - No Film School; Scott Myers]. In the persona operation the want is the visible pursuit each reel shows — the destination reached, the acquisition, the achievement, the arrival. The want is what a cold viewer can read in one muted watch: this person is going somewhere, getting something, becoming something. Every recurring format instantiates the want (the come-with-me arrival IS the want in motion). The want must be concrete and repeatable per post; it is deliberately shallow on its own — pure flex — which is why the need node exists above it. Author one written want per persona (e.g. 'reaches the world's most exclusive places' / 'builds a life of unhurried taste') before any format work.

included: the want as external conscious plot-driving goal
one written want per persona
the want as the per-reel visible layer
excluded: the need and its arc-level revelation (its own node)
wardrobe/casting mechanics that depict the want (character/wardrobe file)

pros.claim: A single written want per persona makes every reel's visible pursuit consistent and instantly legible to cold viewers
pros.example: each male-persona post showing motion toward exclusive places, so the feed reads as one pursuit rather than random luxury clips

cons.claim: A want alone is pure flex and produces envy without bonding, so it cannot carry the account by itself
cons.example: a feed of arrivals and acquisitions with no underlying value that audiences bond to, plateauing as aspirational wallpaper

failure_modes: leaving the want implicit so different posts imply different pursuits and the feed loses its through-line
writing the want as an abstract value (that is the need's job) so no reel can depict it concretely
acceptance_tests: each persona has one written, concrete, visually depictable want, and the analysis distinguishes it from the need by timescale (want per reel, need across the series)
revisit_triggers: a format is added that cannot depict the written want
audience readings of the feed diverge from the intended pursuit
the owner repositions a persona's storyworld

base.update_signal: a repositioning of a persona or a format that cannot show the want changes the written want

nodes.definition: Define each persona's need: the internal, often unconscious lesson or value — want drives plot, need drives the arc [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine - No Film School; Scott Myers]. In the persona operation the need is the underlying value the brand stands for (freedom, self-mastery, taste) revealed across the series, never stated in one post. Per-reel you show the want; across posts you reveal the need. The need is what makes an audience bond rather than just envy — it converts aspirational wallpaper into a persona people follow for what they stand for [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]. The revelation is paced: early posts establish the aspirational world and the want, a mid-series turn complicates it, and the need surfaces over time through shown choices (what the persona declines, lingers on, returns to), never through confessional captions — which would collide with the aloofness register.

included: the need as arc-level value revelation
the pacing (establish want early, mid-series turn, need surfaces over time)
revelation through shown choices not statements
excluded: the want's per-reel depiction (its own node)
audience-psychology mechanics of parasocial bonding (media-manager/psychology file)

pros.claim: A paced need-revelation gives the feed a spine beyond disconnected flexes and rewards long-term followers
pros.example: the female persona repeatedly shown choosing craft over crowds until 'unhurried taste' reads as her value without ever being captioned

cons.claim: The need is invisible in any single post, so its payoff is slow and unmeasurable in per-post metrics
cons.example: a strategy review judging the need arc a failure because no individual reel's numbers move when it advances

failure_modes: stating the need explicitly in a caption ('freedom is my value') — tell-not-show that also breaks aloofness
never advancing the arc so the feed stays pure flex and audiences engage but do not bond
acceptance_tests: each persona has one written need distinct from its want, a paced revelation plan (early want, mid turn, need surfacing), and the rule that the need is shown through choices, never captioned as a statement
revisit_triggers: audience comments start naming the value (the arc is landing — advance the phase)
a bible review finds recent posts contradict the written need
the owner changes what the brand should stand for

base.update_signal: audience value-naming in comments or an owner repositioning changes the need or its pacing

nodes.definition: Enforce the muted-first-exposure constraint on all story design. The much-cited figure — ~85% of Facebook video watched without sound — comes from Digiday (Sahil Patel, May 17 2016) and is a publisher-reported range (LittleThings ~85%, Mic ~85% of 30-second views, MEC clients ~85-90%), not a single platform-measured statistic: carry it as [FACT-of-attribution / ESTIMATE-of-generality], a 2016 publisher-specific figure never to be presented as a current universal metric [FACT about the sourcing]. The load-bearing implication is independent of the exact percentage: a large majority of first-exposure viewing is muted, so the story must be fully legible with the sound off — expression, body language, action, environment and on-screen text/captions deliver the story; a bold text hook works in seconds 0-2 when audio does not play. Show-not-tell follows: replace stated emotion with depicted behavior — do not caption 'she's confident', show the unhurried walk and the direct gaze [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine].

included: the 85%-muted figure with its full attribution caveat
the design-for-muted implication and text-hook layer
show-not-tell as depicted behavior
excluded: voiceover handling under the constraint (its own node)
caption typography and text-overlay design (design specialist)

pros.claim: Designing every story beat for muted playback makes the reel work for the large majority who never unmute, with sound as pure upside
pros.example: a quote-over-cinematic post whose meaning is complete from the text and imagery alone, gaining nothing-to-lose from the score

cons.claim: The 85% anchor is a 2016 publisher-reported figure, so treating it as a precise current metric over-claims what is actually known
cons.example: a strategy document citing '85% of viewers are muted' as a live platform statistic and failing an honesty audit

failure_modes: letting a spoken line carry a story beat so muted viewers lose the plot
quoting the 85% figure as a current platform-measured fact instead of a 2016 publisher-reported range
acceptance_tests: the analysis quotes the muted figure with the Digiday-2016 publisher-reported caveat, states the story-legible-muted rule, and gives the text-hook and show-not-tell consequences
revisit_triggers: a current platform-measured muted-viewing statistic becomes available
the operation adds a sound-on-first surface
an audit finds posts whose meaning depends on audio

base.update_signal: a current muted-viewing measurement or a sound-on surface changes the constraint's weight

nodes.definition: Lock the status register to quiet luxury. Han, Nunes & Dreze (2010), 'Signaling Status with Luxury Goods: The Role of Brand Prominence', Journal of Marketing 74:15-30, introduces brand prominence (how conspicuous the logo/mark is) and a four-group taxonomy: Patricians (wealthy, low need for status — pay a premium for quiet signals only insiders recognize), Parvenus (wealthy, high need for status — loud conspicuous signals), Proletarians (do not signal), Poseurs (aspirational, counterfeit the parvenu look); empirically, loud prominently-branded status goods averaged cheaper than quiet ones in a study of 465 Gucci/LV handbags [FACT - source 15]. The owner's classic-luxurious aesthetic maps to the Patrician quiet-luxury register: understated tailoring, no loud logos, materials-and-craft over branding, if-you-know-you-know [ESTIMATE grounded in the FACT taxonomy]. The want must therefore be depicted in quiet signals — texture, cut, setting — and the Parvenu/Poseur register (giant logos, obvious flash) is banned because it reads as lower status and new money to the in-group audience.

included: the brand-prominence construct and four-group taxonomy with the loud-cheaper finding
the Patrician mapping of classic-luxurious
the quiet-signal depiction rule for the want
excluded: wardrobe capsule construction and garment prompts (character/wardrobe file)
audience attraction psychology (media-manager/psychology file)

pros.claim: The Patrician register is a research-backed positioning: quiet signals read as higher status to in-group audiences than loud branding
pros.example: depicting wealth through a hand on unlogo'd saddle leather and architectural setting rather than a monogram wall

cons.claim: Quiet signals are only legible to viewers with the decoding knowledge, so the register can under-communicate status to a broad cold audience
cons.example: a mass viewer reading an understated cashmere-and-stone frame as merely pleasant while missing the wealth signal a logo would have shouted

failure_modes: letting generated wardrobe or props drift into visible large logos and monograms (parvenu register)
citing the loud-cheaper handbag finding beyond its scope (one 2010 two-brand study) as a universal law of luxury pricing
acceptance_tests: the analysis names the paper, the four groups, and the 465-handbag loud-cheaper finding, maps classic-luxurious to the Patrician register, and states the no-loud-logos depiction rule
revisit_triggers: a generated asset audit finds logo/branding drift in the feed
the owner's aesthetic brief changes register
the wardrobe specialist needs the register translated into concrete garment rules

base.update_signal: register drift in generated assets or an owner aesthetic change re-opens the register lock

nodes.definition: Deploy mystery and aloofness as luxury-persona devices. Scarcity of self-disclosure is a status signal — the persona that reveals less reads as more exclusive [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]. The concrete device set: restrained, near-micro expression (a flicker of a smile, a barely-there brow flash, a gaze that softens for a beat — restraint reads as class, broad expressions read as trying-too-hard [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine; AU-level phrasing belongs to the expression KB]); gaze control (looking away, or a cool direct gaze rather than an eager one); not explaining (letting the image stand without justifying captions); and controlled reveal (the face partially obscured, the back-to-camera contemplative shot). Aloofness and non-revelation share the same visual grammar as quiet luxury — both withhold rather than shout. The tension with the need arc is real: the persona must withhold per post yet stand for something across the series, resolved by revealing the need through shown choices, never disclosure.

included: the four device families (restrained expression, gaze control, not explaining, controlled reveal)
restraint-reads-as-class as the acting register
the shared withholding grammar with quiet luxury
excluded: FACS AU phrasing for prompts (expression/prompting KB)
any use of obscuring to evoke a real person (closed lane, guarded by its own node)

pros.claim: Withholding devices make the personas read as exclusive and give the feed a consistent cool register that broad mugging would destroy
pros.example: a back-to-camera contemplative shot over a city at dusk with no caption explanation, reading as someone who does not need to perform

cons.claim: Sustained aloofness can starve audience bonding and read as cold if the need arc never surfaces warmth through choices
cons.example: months of unreadable gazes with no shown value, leaving followers admiring but unattached

failure_modes: over-expressing (broad grins, eager gazes) and breaking the register into trying-too-hard
using the controlled-reveal device on imagery styled to suggest a specific real person — a closed-lane breach handled by the guard node
acceptance_tests: the analysis lists all four device families with concrete visual examples and states the restraint-reads-as-class register, tagged as craft doctrine not measured fact
revisit_triggers: audience feedback reads the personas as cold rather than exclusive
the expression KB changes its restrained-expression prompt grammar
a controlled-reveal concept approaches any real-person association

base.update_signal: cold-read audience feedback or a prompt-grammar change in the expression KB retunes the device set

nodes.definition: Keep the likeness lane closed. The non-revelation grammar (obscured face, back-to-camera, partial framing) exists ONLY for the two original personas' mystique. No post, prompt, styling choice, location pairing, caption or hashtag may be designed to evoke a specific real person while hiding the face — the grounding file notes the owner's famous-people/face-not-revealed idea and explicitly routes its legal boundary to the media-manager/legal research file; this KB carries only the prohibition, and no workaround guidance exists or may be authored here. Operationally: every controlled-reveal concept is checked against the question 'would a reasonable viewer read this as person X?' — signature hairstyles, iconic wardrobe, known locations-plus-context, or caption winks all count as evocation even with the face hidden. If the answer is yes or unclear, the concept is killed, not adjusted toward deniability. The devices of the aloofness node remain fully available for the original personas.

included: the absolute prohibition on evoking a specific real person while hiding the face
the reasonable-viewer evocation test over styling, context and captions
kill-not-adjust handling of flagged concepts
excluded: the legal analysis itself (legal research file)
generic celebrity-adjacent aesthetics that evoke no specific person

pros.claim: An absolute, checkable guard removes the operation's most dangerous failure mode before any asset is generated
pros.example: killing a 'mystery icon at the villa' concept at the brief stage because the styling reads as a specific singer, instead of arguing deniability after posting

cons.claim: The reasonable-viewer test is judgment-based and will kill some borderline concepts that were legally and creatively fine
cons.example: dropping a back-to-camera tailored-suit frame because one reviewer saw a resemblance no audience would

failure_modes: treating a hidden face as sufficient deniability while styling and context still evoke a specific person
adjusting a flagged concept toward plausible deniability instead of killing it
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the lane is closed with no workaround guidance, gives the reasonable-viewer evocation test covering styling/context/captions, and mandates kill-not-adjust for flagged concepts
revisit_triggers: any new concept involves an obscured or partially framed figure
the legal research file updates the boundary
a published post draws real-person comparison comments

base.update_signal: a legal-file boundary update or real-person comparison comments on a post re-trigger the guard review

nodes.definition: Author the small set of named recurring formats the personas cycle through — recurring formats build viewer expectation and lower production cost [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]. The grounded library: (1) 'Come with me' — first-person POV travel/luxury arrival with an awe payoff, leveraging aspiration proximity; (2) Transformation/reveal — before-to-after outfit or plain-to-destination using the escalation-then-payoff shape; (3) Quote-over-cinematic — the owner's stated motivational pillar: a motivational line as text over a cinematic luxury clip, meaning carried in silent autoplay with the quote as the text hook; (4) 'A day / a place' — episodic slice-of-life in the persona's world with mystery/aloofness maintained; (5) Dual-persona interplay — the male and female personas in complementary or paired formats, a recurring relational thread the audience follows. Every format must pass the muted-legibility constraint by construction, and each carries its own default emotional lever (awe, curiosity, aspiration) and ending mode assigned downstream.

included: the five named formats with their emotional levers
expectation-building and production-cost rationales
muted legibility as a per-format admission test
excluded: shot lists and transition grammar per format (camera/editing file)
the per-format ending-mode assignment (its own node)

pros.claim: A named library turns each post into an instance of a rehearsed template, building audience expectation while cutting per-post design cost
pros.example: followers recognizing a 'come with me' opening frame instantly and staying for the known arrival payoff

cons.claim: A fixed library can go stale, and formats repeated without variation train the audience to skip
cons.example: the fifth identical transformation reel in a month holding worse than the first as the payoff becomes predictable

failure_modes: inventing one-off concepts per post so no expectation ever builds and every post pays full design cost
adding a format that only works with sound and fails muted first exposure
acceptance_tests: the analysis names all five grounded formats with their emotional levers and rationales, and states that muted legibility is an admission requirement for any format
revisit_triggers: a format underperforms across multiple consecutive instances
a new format candidate is proposed
the duo arc requires a format the library lacks

base.update_signal: format-level performance trends or a duo-arc gap changes the library composition

nodes.definition: Design episodic hooks that convert single-view curiosity into follows. Grounding: Loewenstein (1994), 'The Psychology of Curiosity', Psychological Bulletin 116(1):75-98 — the information-gap theory: curiosity is cognitively induced deprivation arising from a perceived gap between what one knows and wants to know, and intensity rises with how fillable the gap feels [FACT - source 5]. Application [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]: end on an unresolved beat (the door not yet opened, the destination not yet named, 'part 2') so the gap stays deliberately unfilled across posts; a numbered series ('Part 1/...', 'Location 3 of 7') makes the gap explicitly fillable-by-following, giving a concrete reason to follow and return. The honesty edge: the gap must eventually fill — over-teasing that never pays off is clickbait and breeds distrust, so every opened loop is logged with its promised payoff and a due post.

included: information-gap grounding for open loops
numbered-series mechanics as fillable-by-following gaps
the every-loop-must-fill honesty rule with a loop log
excluded: the hard-loop alternative and the per-format choice (its own node)
comment/DM community management around the tease (media manager)

pros.claim: An explicitly numbered open loop converts a moment of curiosity into a follow because the gap is visibly fillable by returning
pros.example: 'Location 3 of 7' ending on an unopened gate, giving the viewer a concrete series to subscribe to rather than a one-off tease

cons.claim: Unfilled or chronically late payoffs invert the device: the audience learns the gaps are bait and stops trusting the tease
cons.example: a 'part 2' promised in the caption that never ships, harvesting distrust comments on every later tease

failure_modes: opening loops with no logged payoff plan so teases silently go unfilled
over-teasing every post until the account reads as clickbait rather than a story
acceptance_tests: the analysis grounds the device in Loewenstein's information-gap theory, gives the numbered-series mechanic, and states the every-opened-loop-gets-a-logged-payoff rule
revisit_triggers: comment sentiment shows tease fatigue or bait accusations
an opened loop's payoff slips past its due post
follow-conversion behavior around numbered series shifts

base.update_signal: tease-fatigue signals or a payoff slip re-opens the loop-discipline rules

nodes.definition: Assign an ending mode to every format: (a) hard loop — the final frame flows back into the first so the restart is invisible; seamless looping is a documented watch-time tactic because viewers rewatch without noticing, and completion/replay signals aid distribution [FACT - documented tactic, source 10]; practical mechanics (match last-frame composition/motion/lighting to the first, end on continuing motion, loop-clean audio) and the suggested 7-10s optimal loop length come from a marketing blog and are directional only [ESTIMATE]; or (b) open loop — the unresolved 'part 2' beat that drives comments and follows instead of rewatches. The two modes trade replay watch-time against follow conversion and cannot both own the same ending. Default assignment [ESTIMATE / craft design]: ambient, non-narrative formats (quote-over-cinematic, a-day/a-place) take hard loops; narrative and numbered-series posts (come-with-me chains, transformations mid-series, crossover episodes) take open loops. The choice is made per format in the bible, not per post ad hoc.

included: hard-loop mechanics and their FACT/ESTIMATE split
the replay-vs-follow trade
the per-format default assignment recorded in the bible
excluded: frame-matching execution and edit mechanics (camera/editing file)
the curiosity-gap theory behind open loops (its own node)

pros.claim: Assigning ending modes per format makes each post's final seconds serve one measurable goal instead of splitting the difference
pros.example: a quote-over-cinematic that loops invisibly for replays while the numbered travel series ends on the unopened gate for follows

cons.claim: A wrong per-format default is systematically wrong across every instance until reviewed
cons.example: hard-looping a numbered series so viewers replay but never get the follow prompt the numbering was built for

failure_modes: ending a post half-looped and half-teased so neither replay nor follow conversion works
choosing endings per post ad hoc so the format's ending behavior never becomes a learnable expectation
acceptance_tests: the analysis states both modes with the hard-loop FACT/ESTIMATE split, names the replay-vs-follow trade, and records a per-format default assignment
revisit_triggers: replay or follow behavior diverges from a format's assigned mode
a format changes narrative role (ambient to serial or back)
loop execution quality issues surface from the edit side

base.update_signal: replay/follow divergence from an assigned mode retunes the per-format table

nodes.definition: Align the series' emotional register with what is actually shared. Berger & Milkman (2012), 'What Makes Online Content Viral?', Journal of Marketing Research — analyzing all NYT articles over ~3 months — found content evoking high-arousal emotions (positive: awe; negative: anger, anxiety) is more viral, while low-arousal deactivating emotions (e.g. sadness) are less viral; positive content is generally more viral than negative, and the result held controlling for surprise, interest, usefulness and placement [FACT - source 6]. Application: luxury travel, architecture and nature reels are awe machines — sweeping reveals, scale, grandeur — and awe is simultaneously aspirational and high-arousal, exactly the sharable quadrant, so the series leans into scale and reveal [ESTIMATE application of the FACT]. Handoff discipline: distribution tactics and ranking signals are the media manager's domain; the story-side commitment is simply that formats bias toward awe-capable payoffs, sourced from environment scale, never from loud branding (which would break the quiet register).

included: the Berger & Milkman finding with its controls
awe as the aspirational high-arousal quadrant
environment-scale sourcing of awe under the quiet register
excluded: ranking-signal tactics and posting strategy (media manager)
reveal-shot execution (camera/editing file)

pros.claim: Awe is the one emotional register that is simultaneously on-brand aspirational and evidenced as the most-shared positive affect
pros.example: a slow aerial reveal of a clifftop estate delivering scale-driven awe that is both luxurious and built to be sent to a friend

cons.claim: The evidence base is NYT article sharing in 2012, so porting it to 2026 vertical video is an analogy, not a measured platform result
cons.example: assuming the awe effect size transfers to reels quantitatively when the study measured email-list article sharing

failure_modes: chasing arousal through spectacle-flash (gold, logos, crowds) that gains energy but breaks the Patrician register
citing the 2012 article-sharing result as if it were a measured reel-platform statistic
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites Berger & Milkman 2012 with the high/low-arousal contrast and controls, applies awe via environment scale and reveal, and flags the article-to-reel transfer as analogy
revisit_triggers: share-per-post patterns contradict the awe bias
the media manager's ranking-signal guidance changes what story should optimize
a format's awe payoff starts requiring register-breaking spectacle

base.update_signal: share-pattern data or new distribution guidance changes the emotional-register bias

nodes.definition: Run the male and female personas as parallel lives: each carries its own written want, its own need arc, its own format rotation and its own feed presence, inside the one shared classic-luxurious genre and signature system. The grounding file establishes the dual-persona operation and the dual-persona-interplay format as a recurring relational thread the audience follows [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]; the parallel-lives elaboration is series-design doctrine built on it [ESTIMATE]: parallelism multiplies story surface (two wants, two arcs, two audiences) without doubling continuity risk, because each storyworld is internally consistent on its own. Design rules: the two wants must be distinct but rhyming (complementary pursuits, not copies); the personas' worlds share the genre register and grade so a viewer of both feeds reads one universe; and neither persona's solo storyline may require watching the other's feed to make sense — parallel, not interleaved.

included: one want/need/format rotation per persona
distinct-but-rhyming wants in a shared register
solo-legibility of each storyline
excluded: crossover events (their own node)
character identity/face consistency mechanics (character/wardrobe file)

pros.claim: Parallel self-contained storyworlds double the operation's narrative surface while keeping each feed legible to its own audience alone
pros.example: the male persona's exclusive-places pursuit and the female persona's unhurried-taste arc each standing alone yet reading as one universe in grade and register

cons.claim: Two arcs mean double the bible upkeep, and drift between the two worlds (grade, register, values) fractures the shared universe
cons.example: the female feed drifting warm-minimal while the male feed stays cool-classic until crossovers look like two different shows

failure_modes: writing the two personas as copies of one want so the duo adds surface without contrast
letting one storyline depend on the other's posts so solo viewers lose the plot
acceptance_tests: the analysis assigns each persona a distinct written want and need, states the shared-register rule, and verifies each storyline is legible without the other feed
revisit_triggers: register or grade drift between the two feeds is detected
audience overlap data shows most followers follow both (weakening the solo-legibility constraint)
the owner adds or retires a persona

base.update_signal: cross-feed drift, audience-overlap data, or a persona roster change reshapes the parallel design

nodes.definition: Design crossovers — posts where both personas appear in one storyline — as scarce, arc-significant events, not a regular fixture. Grounding: the dual-persona-interplay recurring format (complementary or paired posts as a relational thread the audience follows) [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]; the scarcity discipline is series-design doctrine [ESTIMATE]: a crossover is an event precisely because the default is parallel lives, so frequency spends the event value. Design rules: crossovers land at arc moments (a series finale, a mid-series turn, a numbered-series payoff), are teased as open loops in both feeds so each audience converts to the other, keep the relational read ambiguous (the mystery register extends to the relationship — companions, rivals, or something unexplained, never confessed), and each crossover must still be legible to a viewer who follows only one feed. The crossover cadence is recorded in the bible and reviewed against performance, not improvised.

included: crossovers as scarce arc-placed events
cross-feed open-loop teasing for mutual audience conversion
relational ambiguity under the mystery register
excluded: the parallel default (its own node)
two-character generation consistency mechanics (character/wardrobe and prompting files)

pros.claim: Scarce crossovers convert each persona's audience to the other and give the duo thread event weight that regular co-appearances would dissipate
pros.example: a two-part crossover teased from both feeds at a series finale, with each feed's open loop resolving in the other's post

cons.claim: Crossovers double production constraints (two consistent characters in one frame) and a botched one damages both storyworlds at once
cons.example: a paired post where the shared scene's grade matches neither feed, reading as off-brand in both

failure_modes: running crossovers so often the parallel storylines collapse into one couple-feed
confessing the relationship in caption and burning the mystery register's ambiguity
acceptance_tests: the analysis places crossovers at arc moments with a recorded cadence, uses cross-feed open loops for mutual conversion, keeps the relational read ambiguous, and preserves single-feed legibility
revisit_triggers: crossover posts start outnumbering solo posts in a cycle
cross-feed conversion around a crossover is measured
audience sentiment demands relational resolution

base.update_signal: crossover frequency creep, conversion measurements, or sentiment pressure retunes the cadence

nodes.definition: Carry the owner's word 'phonics' as a named [UNKNOWN]. The word appears in the owner's story-levels list ('phonics, expressions, emotions, how they express...') and is a speech-to-text artifact [UNKNOWN - artifact, grounding file section 7]. Most probable intended meanings: (a) phonetics / voice delivery for voiceover, or (b) a mis-transcription of some other delivery concept. This KB proceeds on reading (a) — voice-delivery basics (pace, pitch, pause) — explicitly flagged as an interpretation, not a certainty. The blocker is named: OWNER CLARIFICATION of what 'phonics' meant. Until it arrives, every voice-delivery node downstream inherits the interpretation flag; no deliverable may present the voice-delivery reading as the owner's confirmed intent, and the bible records the word verbatim with its artifact status so the ambiguity is never silently laundered into fact.

included: the verbatim owner word and its artifact status
the two candidate readings and the chosen interpretation flag
the named owner-clarification blocker
excluded: the voice-delivery content itself (downstream nodes)
re-interviewing mechanics for the owner (operations, not this KB)

pros.claim: Naming the unknown keeps the operation honest: work proceeds on a flagged interpretation instead of a silently invented owner intent
pros.example: the bible entry reading "'phonics' [UNKNOWN artifact] -> interpreted as voice delivery, pending owner confirmation" rather than asserting the owner asked for voiceover direction

cons.claim: Proceeding on interpretation risks sunk work if the owner meant something else entirely
cons.example: a library of voice-delivery direction built on reading (a) being shelved when the owner clarifies they meant on-screen text styling

failure_modes: dropping the flag and presenting voice-delivery direction as the owner's confirmed request
never surfacing the question to the owner so the unknown persists indefinitely
acceptance_tests: every deliverable touching voice delivery carries the interpretation flag, the bible records the verbatim word with [UNKNOWN artifact] status, and the owner-clarification blocker is named as the resolution path
revisit_triggers: the owner clarifies the word (either reading)
a new transcript or brief from the owner uses the word again in context
a deliverable is found presenting the interpretation as confirmed intent

base.update_signal: owner clarification of 'phonics' resolves the unknown and re-scopes the voice group

nodes.definition: Position the voiceover correctly under the muted constraint: the voiceover and score are an enhancement for the minority who unmute, never the load-bearer of the story. Consequences [grounded in the 2016 Digiday reporting and its craft adaptations]: (1) caption spoken content — if a persona 'says' something it must appear as text, which also serves accessibility; (2) design a sound-on payoff (the score drop, a whispered line) as a reason to unmute — a bonus, never a dependency; (3) every voiceover reel must pass a mute test: watched silent, the story must be complete. This rule is the bridge between the silent-legibility constraint and the delivery craft: pace, pitch and pause direction only matter for the unmuted minority, so they are polish on top of a visually complete story, and no story beat may be assigned to the voice track alone. Delivery direction is handed to the audio specialist's tooling; this KB supplies the direction, not the tools.

included: the enhancement-not-load-bearer rule
caption-spoken-content and sound-on-payoff consequences
the mute test as the acceptance check
excluded: voice generation tools and parameters (audio specialist)
caption typography (design specialist)

pros.claim: Treating voice as bonus makes every reel robust to the muted majority while still rewarding the unmuted minority
pros.example: a voiceover reel whose captioned lines carry the story silent, with the whispered delivery as a discovered pleasure on unmute

cons.claim: Captioning every spoken line adds a text layer that must be designed, and doubles the places a script change touches
cons.example: a late script edit requiring both the regenerated voice track and the re-set caption cards

failure_modes: assigning a plot beat to the voice track alone so muted viewers lose the story
skipping captions on spoken content and failing both the muted majority and accessibility
acceptance_tests: every voiceover reel passes the mute test (story complete with sound off), all spoken content is captioned, and any sound-on payoff is verified to be a bonus rather than a dependency
revisit_triggers: a mute-test failure surfaces in review
unmute-rate signals become available and change the polish/robustness balance
the caption layer conflicts with the text-hook layer in the same frame

base.update_signal: unmute-rate data or repeated mute-test failures rebalance voice investment

nodes.definition: Set voiceover pace from the FACT anchors: average conversational English runs ~150 wpm (National Center for Voice and Speech, via source 16); most adults sit 120-150 wpm in conversation; audiobook/podcast narration — rehearsed, clearly enunciated — runs ~150-160 wpm [FACT - source 16]. The reel-specific direction is craft calibration on those anchors [ESTIMATE]: aim for the ~140-160 wpm band to sound natural but crisp; below ~130 wpm reads as ponderous, above ~170 wpm as rushed. Operational use: word-budget every script before generation — a 20-second voiceover at 150 wpm is ~50 words — and when a script overruns its duration, cut words rather than accelerate delivery, because pushing past ~170 wpm buys length at the cost of the unhurried register the personas require. The band applies to spoken phrases; deliberate pauses are governed by their own node and do not count against the band.

included: the NCVS/conversation/narration wpm anchors
the 140-160 reel band with ponderous/rushed edges
word-budgeting and cut-not-accelerate
excluded: pause placement (its own node)
voice tool parameters and generation mechanics (audio specialist)

pros.claim: A word-budgeted script hits its duration at a natural rate instead of being rescued by unnatural delivery speed
pros.example: trimming a 70-word draft to 50 words for a 20-second slot so the read sits at ~150 wpm instead of a rushed 210

cons.claim: The reel band is craft calibration, not a measured optimum, and register may justify slower-than-band delivery
cons.example: a deliberately weighty 125-wpm read suiting a contemplative crossover finale despite sitting below the band

failure_modes: accelerating delivery past ~170 wpm to fit an overlong script instead of cutting words
treating the 140-160 band as a measured platform fact rather than calibration on the FACT anchors
acceptance_tests: every voiceover script is word-budgeted against its duration at the band rate, and the analysis separates the FACT wpm anchors from the ESTIMATE reel band
revisit_triggers: the owner clarifies 'phonics' and re-scopes voice work
delivery feedback finds the band wrong for the persona register
scripts systematically overrun their slots

base.update_signal: phonics clarification or register feedback recalibrates the band

nodes.definition: Direct pitch for the luxury-authority register [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine throughout]: vary pitch to avoid monotone; a slight downward inflection at phrase ends reads as authoritative and confident (a statement), while rising ends read as uncertain or questioning. For the personas — whose register is unhurried, assured, Patrician — favor grounded, lower-register, downward-resolving delivery: phrases that settle rather than lift, no uptalk, no eager brightness. This is the vocal twin of the aloofness devices: the voice withholds excitement the way the face withholds expression, so delivery direction and expression direction must agree (an eager, rising read over a restrained cool gaze is a register clash). The direction is craft doctrine, not phonetics research — carried as such — and it is delivery guidance handed to voice generation, not a claim about listener psychology.

included: pitch variation against monotone
downward-resolving phrase ends and lower register
agreement between vocal and facial restraint
excluded: voice cloning/model selection (audio specialist)
FACS-level expression direction (expression KB)

pros.claim: Downward-resolving low-register delivery makes the voiceover reinforce the aloof Patrician register instead of fighting it
pros.example: a travel-arrival line read as a settled statement over the reveal, matching the persona's cool gaze rather than selling it

cons.claim: Uniform downward resolution across every line risks a flat, portentous read that tips from assured into self-serious
cons.example: six consecutive settling phrases making a 30-second voiceover sound like a movie-trailer parody

failure_modes: uptalking phrase ends and undercutting the authority register
directing pitch as if the authority reading were established listener psychology rather than craft doctrine
acceptance_tests: voiceover direction specifies varied pitch with downward-resolving phrase ends in a lower register, checks agreement with the visual restraint register, and tags the guidance as craft doctrine
revisit_triggers: delivery feedback reads the voice as flat or self-serious
a persona's register shifts
the expression KB changes its restraint grammar in ways the voice must mirror

base.update_signal: delivery feedback or a register shift retunes the pitch direction

nodes.definition: Direct pauses as structure [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine throughout]: strategic silence before a key word or before the payoff creates emphasis and lets a muted-to-unmuted viewer catch up; pauses also let the visual breathe. In a stitched reel, align pauses with cut points — the voice falls silent across the transition and re-enters on the new shot, so the edit rhythm and the delivery rhythm reinforce each other instead of colliding mid-word. The payoff pause is the highest-value placement: a beat of silence before the final line or the reveal-synchronized word gives the climax air. Pauses are deliberate delivery content, not dead time: they do not count against the wpm band (which governs spoken phrases), and when duration pressure hits, spoken words are cut before pauses are compressed — a pause-less luxury read is rushed by construction.

included: pre-payoff and pre-keyword silence
pause-to-cut-point alignment in stitched reels
pauses as content excluded from the wpm band
excluded: the cut points themselves (camera/editing file)
score/silence interplay (audio/soundtrack file)

pros.claim: Cut-aligned pauses make delivery and edit rhythm reinforce each other and give the payoff air instead of narration wall-to-wall
pros.example: silence across the whip-pan into the villa reveal, with the final line landing one beat after the image

cons.claim: Pauses spend scarce seconds in a 15-60s format, so each one must earn its beat
cons.example: three reverent pauses in a 15-second reel leaving only nine seconds of actual content

failure_modes: running narration continuously across cuts so delivery and edit rhythm collide
compressing pauses to fit an overlong script instead of cutting words
acceptance_tests: voiceover direction places a pre-payoff pause, aligns mid-reel pauses with cut points, and the script edit log shows words were cut before pauses when duration pressure hit
revisit_triggers: the edit grid changes a reel's cut points after voice generation
pacing feedback finds the read airless or over-paused
a format's payoff structure changes

base.update_signal: edit-grid changes or pacing feedback retunes pause placement

nodes.definition: Install recurring visual signatures as the series' narrative glue. The owner's hard requirements — consistent character, consistent wardrobe capsule, consistent classic-luxurious genre — are what let disconnected reels read as one ongoing story; recurring visual signatures (a color grade, a location type, a recurring object or wardrobe piece) function as the series' brand, reinforcing the arc [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine, grounding section 8.3]. This node owns the NARRATIVE function of consistency — the mechanics of face/identity and wardrobe generation belong to the character/wardrobe file. The signature set is small and named: one grade family, a recurring location type per persona, and one or two totem objects (the watch put down on marble, the same coat over the shoulder) that recur across posts as continuity anchors a follower learns to spot. Signatures also serve the muted constraint: they are instant, silent identifiers that a cold scroll can recognize before any text or sound.

included: the named signature set (grade family, location type, totem objects)
signatures as continuity anchors and silent identifiers
the narrative function of consistency
excluded: face/identity and wardrobe generation mechanics (character/wardrobe file)
grade execution (camera/editing and design files)

pros.claim: A small named signature set makes any single frame attributable to the series, turning consistency from a constraint into recognition equity
pros.example: the recurring coat-over-shoulder totem letting a follower identify the persona in a half-second cold scroll before any caption loads

cons.claim: Signatures harden over time: changing the grade or retiring a totem later breaks the very continuity they built
cons.example: a mid-series grade refresh making the back catalog visibly discontinuous with new posts

failure_modes: accumulating unnamed, accidental signatures no one governs so continuity depends on luck
changing a signature without an arc reason and silently breaking the series' visual identity
acceptance_tests: the bible names the signature set (grade family, location types, totem objects per persona) and every published post is checkable against it
revisit_triggers: a proposed post cannot carry the signature set
a signature change is proposed (requires an arc-level justification)
the character/wardrobe file changes what is generable consistently

base.update_signal: a generability change or an arc-justified signature revision updates the set

nodes.definition: Maintain the series bible as the single governance document every post is authored against, so the story stays genre-consistent classic-luxurious. Contents [ESTIMATE / craft discipline]: per-persona want and need with the arc phase each is in; the quiet-Patrician register rules (no loud logos, texture/cut/setting over branding); the recurring-format library with each format's emotional lever and assigned ending mode; the signature set; the duo map (parallel wants, crossover cadence, open-loop ledger with due payoffs); the voice-delivery direction with the 'phonics' [UNKNOWN artifact] flag carried verbatim; and the honesty register — every empirical claim the operation relies on recorded with its FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tag (the 2016 muted figure's caveat, the 2012 sharing study's scope, the contested items staying contested). The bible is versioned: changes require an entry with a reason, so drift is a recorded decision, never an accident. A post that contradicts the bible is wrong by definition until the bible itself is deliberately amended.

included: the bible's full content list
versioned-change discipline
the honesty register carrying every claim's tag
excluded: character/wardrobe generation specs (their file, referenced not duplicated)
the per-post gate that enforces the bible (its own node)

pros.claim: A versioned bible makes genre consistency enforceable: any post can be checked against one document, and drift becomes a visible recorded decision
pros.example: catching a warm-toned, logo-visible draft because it contradicts the register and grade pages of the bible before generation spend

cons.claim: The bible is overhead that must be kept current; a stale bible enforces yesterday's story and blocks legitimate evolution
cons.example: a retired format still listed as canon causing a correct new-format post to fail review

failure_modes: letting the bible go stale so enforcement diverges from the actual creative direction
laundering an [ESTIMATE] or [UNKNOWN] into the bible as plain fact, losing the honesty tag
acceptance_tests: the bible contains all listed sections including the honesty register and the verbatim 'phonics' [UNKNOWN] flag, every change has a versioned entry with a reason, and a sampled recent post checks clean against it
revisit_triggers: any node upstream changes (register, formats, signatures, arc, voice direction)
a gate failure traces to a bible gap or staleness
the owner issues new creative direction

base.update_signal: any upstream node change, gate-failure pattern, or owner direction triggers a versioned bible update

nodes.definition: Plot the series arc as a beat map across posts: which post advances which persona's arc, where the open loops sit, and when the need surfaces. Per the arc-migration principle, the hero's-journey skeleton and the want-to-need revelation spread across the feed [ESTIMATE / craft doctrine]: early posts establish the ordinary/aspirational world and the want; a mid-series turn complicates it; the need (the value the persona stands for) surfaces over time through shown choices. The beat map is a working calendar-agnostic sequence (cadence and timing belong to the media manager): post N is a want-beat in format X, post N+2 opens a numbered loop, post N+5 is the crossover that pays two loops at once, and so on. Each beat entry names its format, its ending mode, its arc function (establish / escalate / turn / surface-need / payoff) and any loop it opens or closes — making arc progress inspectable instead of vibes, and giving the gate something concrete to check each post against.

included: the beat-map sequence with per-post arc function, format, ending mode and loop ledger
the establish/turn/surface-need pacing
arc progress as an inspectable artifact
excluded: posting cadence and timing (media manager)
per-post shot design (camera/editing file)

pros.claim: A beat map makes the invisible series arc a checkable artifact: every post knows its arc function and every opened loop has a scheduled payoff
pros.example: seeing at a glance that the numbered travel series' loop from post 12 pays off in post 15, and that the female persona's need has not advanced in eight posts

cons.claim: A rigid beat map resists reactive opportunities (a trending sound, a spontaneous location) that reels reward
cons.example: declining a perfectly on-brand spontaneous concept because the map says post 14 must be the mid-series turn

failure_modes: planning beats without arc functions so the map is a content calendar, not a story
letting the map fossilize instead of re-sequencing when a beat over- or under-performs
acceptance_tests: every planned post has an arc function, format, ending mode, and loop entries; opened loops all have due payoffs; and each persona's need-surfacing beats appear at the planned rhythm
revisit_triggers: a beat lands differently than planned (audience reads it as a turn, or misses it)
an open loop's payoff slips
the crossover cadence changes

base.update_signal: beat-landing feedback, loop slips, or cadence changes re-sequence the map

nodes.definition: Run every episode through the go/no-go gate before generation spend and again before posting. The checklist composes the upstream nodes: (1) bible check — register, signatures, format canon, persona want/need phase all consistent; (2) arc check — the post has a named arc function on the beat map and its loop entries (opened/closed) are logged; (3) ending check — the ending matches the format's assigned mode, and any 'part 2' promise has a due payoff; (4) likeness check — no obscured-figure concept evokes a specific real person (kill, not adjust, on a flag); (5) mute check — the story is complete with sound off, spoken content captioned; (6) voice check (if voiceover) — script word-budgeted to the pace band, pauses cut-aligned, the phonics interpretation flag carried; (7) honesty check — any empirical claim in caption or internal notes carries its tag. A post failing any check is fixed or dropped; a check failing repeatedly for the same reason escalates to a bible amendment rather than serial exceptions.

included: the seven-point checklist and its two run points (pre-generation, pre-post)
fix-or-drop handling
the repeated-failure-escalates-to-bible rule
excluded: generation execution and asset QC (prompting/production specialists)
post-publication analytics review (media manager, feeding the iteration protocol)

pros.claim: One composed gate catches register, arc, ending, likeness, mute, voice and honesty failures before they cost generation spend or a published mistake
pros.example: a draft failing the mute check and the loop ledger in one review, fixed for a fraction of the cost of a posted retraction

cons.claim: A seven-point gate on every post adds friction and invites rubber-stamping if failures rarely occur
cons.example: reviewers skimming the likeness check after fifty clean posts, exactly when a borderline concept slips through

failure_modes: running the gate only pre-post so failures are found after generation spend
handling repeated identical failures as one-off exceptions instead of amending the bible
acceptance_tests: every published post has a completed gate record at both run points, and any check that failed three times for the same reason has a corresponding bible amendment or an explicit decision not to amend
revisit_triggers: a failure class the checklist misses reaches publication
gate friction measurably delays the posting pipeline
any upstream node changes its rule set

base.update_signal: an escaped failure class or upstream rule change amends the checklist

edges.why_related: the want is the per-reel beat layer of the account-level story, so the beat/arc split must be fixed before the want is written
the need is defined against the want (want drives plot, need drives the arc), so the want must exist first
the register rules govern how the want is depicted, so the depicted pursuit must be defined before its signal register is locked
aloofness extends the quiet register from objects to behavior — the withholding grammar presupposes the Patrician positioning
the guard exists because the aloofness toolkit contains obscured-face devices that could otherwise drift toward real-person evocation
formats are the repeatable beat types of the account-level story, so the beat frame precedes the library
muted legibility is an admission requirement for every format in the library
episodic hooks are installed on specific formats (numbered series live inside format instances), so the library precedes the hook design
ending modes are assigned per format, so the format list must exist before the assignment table
the open-loop device is one of the two ending options the choice arbitrates, so it must be defined first
the awe bias is applied to the formats' payoffs, so the library precedes the emotional-register alignment
parallel lives means one want/need arc per persona, so the want/need machinery must exist before it is instantiated twice
a crossover is only an event because the default is parallel lives; the default must be established first
crossovers are teased as cross-feed open loops, so the loop device precedes the crossover design
the enhancement rule is the direct consequence of the muted constraint applied to the voice track
all voice-delivery work proceeds under the phonics interpretation flag, which the pace direction inherits
pace direction is polish on a voice track already positioned as enhancement; the positioning comes first
pitch direction only matters once the voice track's enhancement role and mute-test primacy are fixed
pause placement presupposes the voiceover's role and the captioned, visually complete story it decorates
signatures are the glue that makes disconnected beats read as the account-level story the frame defines
the bible records each persona's want/need and arc phase, so the arcs must be authored before they are governed
the bible's register pages encode the Patrician quiet-luxury rules
the bible canonizes the format library with each format's lever and ending mode
the bible names and versions the signature set
the beat map paces the need revelation, so the need and its phases must exist before they are sequenced
the beat map carries the loop ledger (where loops open and pay off), so the loop device precedes the map
the gate's first check is consistency with the bible, which must therefore exist and be current
the gate's arc check verifies the post against the beat map's function and loop entries
the gate's ending check enforces the per-format ending-mode table
the gate's likeness check runs the guard's reasonable-viewer test on every obscured-figure concept
aloofness withholds self-disclosure while the need arc must reveal what the persona stands for — withholding versus bonding
edges.resolution_rule: aloofness governs the per-post surface; the need is revealed only through shown choices across the arc, never through confessional disclosure — if a single post must choose, stay aloof and let the arc carry the need

edges.why_related: awe wants scale and spectacle while the Patrician register bans loud flash — arousal versus understatement
edges.resolution_rule: source awe from environment scale (architecture, nature, reveal) which satisfies both; where spectacle would require loud branding or flash, the quiet register wins unconditionally

edges.why_related: every crossover spends the independence that makes parallel lives legible solo — event value versus storyline autonomy
edges.resolution_rule: parallel independence wins by default: crossovers stay scarce, land only at arc moments, and if crossover count approaches solo count in any cycle the next crossovers are cut

edges.why_related: pauses spend seconds the wpm budget wants for words — silence versus script length
edges.resolution_rule: the band governs spoken phrases only and pauses are protected content: under duration pressure cut words, never compress the pre-payoff pause to raise effective wpm

edges.why_related: the guard restricts the aloofness toolkit's obscured-face devices whenever a concept approaches real-person evocation
edges.resolution_rule: the guard wins absolutely and unconditionally: a flagged concept is killed, not adjusted toward deniability; non-revelation grammar remains available only for the original personas

edges.why_related: repeated gate failures for the same reason escalate into versioned bible amendments, closing the governance loop
observed share performance of awe-biased payoffs feeds back into which formats stay in the library and how their payoffs are built
aloofness/non-revelation and quiet luxury are the same withholding visual grammar applied to behavior and to objects respectively
recurring signatures are what cause disconnected reels to read as one ongoing story — the mechanism behind the account-as-story frame

conflict_axes.name: per_reel_want_vs_series_need
conflict_axes.description: Each post wants to show the visible pursuit (flex, arrival, acquisition) while the account needs to reveal an underlying value over time; over-serving the want yields envy without bonding, over-serving the need yields preachy posts no cold viewer stays for.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: want carries every individual post; the need advances only through shown choices at the beat-map rhythm — never captioned as a statement

conflict_axes.name: quiet_patrician_vs_loud_spectacle
conflict_axes.description: The classic-luxurious register demands quiet insider signals (texture, cut, setting) while attention and awe pull toward loud spectacle; the Han/Nunes/Dreze taxonomy says loud signals read as lower-status parvenu to the in-group.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the register wins on objects and branding; arousal is sourced from environment scale and reveal, which is awe without flash

conflict_axes.name: hard_loop_replay_vs_open_loop_follow
conflict_axes.description: A seamless loop maximizes replays and watch time per view; an open loop converts curiosity into comments and follows — one ending cannot do both jobs.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: assign per format in the bible: ambient formats loop, narrative/numbered formats tease — and never post a half-looped half-teased ending

conflict_axes.name: aloof_withholding_vs_audience_bonding
conflict_axes.description: Mystery and restraint make the personas read exclusive, but sustained non-disclosure starves the bonding the need arc exists to create.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: withhold on the surface, reveal through choices: gaze and caption stay aloof while what the persona repeatedly chooses shows the value

conflict_axes.name: format_repeatability_vs_novelty
conflict_axes.description: Recurring formats build expectation and cut cost but decay toward predictable-skip; constant novelty resets audience learning and pays full production cost every post.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the library small and vary the instance (location, escalation, payoff) inside a stable format shell; retire or refresh a format on sustained decay, via the bible

conflict_axes.name: crossover_event_vs_parallel_autonomy
conflict_axes.description: Duo crossovers create event weight and cross-feed conversion but each one spends the storyline independence that keeps both feeds legible solo.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: crossovers only at arc moments with a recorded cadence; if crossover count approaches solo count in a cycle, cut the next ones

conflict_axes.name: muted_load_bearing_vs_sound_on_craft
conflict_axes.description: The muted majority requires the story to be complete silent, while voiceover craft (pace, pitch, pause) invests in the unmuted minority's experience.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: mute test first, always: voice work is polish on a visually complete story, and no plot beat may live only on the voice track

conflict_axes.name: proceed_on_interpretation_vs_wait_for_clarification
conflict_axes.description: The 'phonics' [UNKNOWN] can be worked around by proceeding on the voice-delivery reading (risking sunk work) or by blocking voice work until the owner clarifies (risking idle scope).
poles: proceed on the flagged voice-delivery reading
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: proceed with the flag carried on every deliverable, keep the clarification request live, and cap investment in interpretation-dependent work until it resolves

conflict_axes.name: bible_consistency_vs_creative_drift
conflict_axes.description: The bible enforces yesterday's recorded decisions while the creative work naturally evolves; unrecorded drift fractures the genre, but a frozen bible blocks legitimate growth.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: drift must become a versioned bible amendment with a reason — evolution is allowed, accidents are not; repeated gate failures for one reason force the amendment question

edge_cases.description: The owner clarifies that 'phonics' meant something other than voice delivery (e.g. on-screen text styling), invalidating the interpretation the voice group was built on
edge_cases.mitigation: the flag was carried on every deliverable, so re-scope the voice group per the clarification and re-file the delivery direction under its true home; the sunk work was capped by design

edge_cases.description: A controlled-reveal concept (obscured face, iconic styling, known location) reads as a specific real person to test viewers
edge_cases.trigger: the reasonable-viewer evocation check flags a draft, or comparison comments appear on a similar published post
edge_cases.mitigation: kill the concept outright — no adjustment toward deniability — and record the trigger pattern in the bible so similar briefs are caught earlier

edge_cases.description: An open loop's promised 'part 2' never ships and tease-fatigue comments accumulate on later posts
edge_cases.trigger: a loop-ledger entry passes its due post unfilled
edge_cases.mitigation: pay off or explicitly close every overdue loop before opening new ones, and gate new teases on a clean ledger

edge_cases.description: Generated wardrobe or props drift into visible logos/monograms, flipping the feed from Patrician to parvenu register
edge_cases.trigger: a register audit or gate check finds branded items in drafts or published posts
edge_cases.mitigation: regenerate the assets under the no-loud-logos rule, and add the offending pattern to the bible's register page so prompting specialists exclude it

edge_cases.description: A numbered narrative series episode is published with a hard loop ending, harvesting replays but never presenting the follow hook the numbering was built for
edge_cases.trigger: ending-mode mismatch between the post and its format's bible assignment
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce the ending check at the pre-generation gate run, and re-cut the ending before posting when caught late

edge_cases.description: A voiceover reel assigns a plot beat to the spoken track alone, so the muted majority loses the story
edge_cases.trigger: the mute test fails in gate review, or comments show muted viewers missing the point
edge_cases.mitigation: caption the line or move the beat into image/action, and re-run the mute test before posting

edge_cases.description: Crossover posts creep from scarce events to the majority of a cycle, collapsing the two parallel storyworlds into one couple-feed
edge_cases.trigger: crossover count approaches or exceeds solo count in a posting cycle
edge_cases.mitigation: cut the next planned crossovers, re-space them to arc moments on the beat map, and record the cadence cap in the bible

edge_cases.description: The need is stated explicitly in a caption ('freedom is everything to me'), simultaneously telling-not-showing and breaking the aloofness register
edge_cases.trigger: a caption draft contains a value statement in the persona's voice
edge_cases.mitigation: strip the statement and encode the value as a shown choice in the imagery; captions stay unexplaining per the aloofness rules

edge_cases.description: A script overruns its reel duration and delivery is accelerated past ~170 wpm to fit, producing a rushed read that breaks the unhurried register
edge_cases.trigger: word count exceeds the duration budget at the band rate and the fix applied is speed, not cuts
